question: Who propounded the concept of ‘Rule of Law’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is AV Dicey.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The concept of the "Rule of Law" was propounded and popularised by the British jurist Professor Albert Venn Dicey (A. V. Dicey) in his classic work "Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution" (1885). (विधि का शासन — ए. वी. डायसी)

• Dicey gave the doctrine three pillars:

◦ Supremacy of law — absence of arbitrary power; no one can be punished except for a distinct breach of law.

◦ Equality before the law — all persons, whatever their rank, are subject to the ordinary law administered by ordinary courts.

◦ Predominance of the legal spirit — the constitution is the result of the ordinary law of the land as developed by the courts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• In India, the Rule of Law has been made a part of Article 14 (equality before the law and equal protection of the laws) and is recognised as a part of the basic structure of the Constitution (Kesavananda Bharati case, 1973; Indira Nehru Gandhi vs Raj Narain, 1975).

• Option 2 C. K. Daphtary was India’s first Attorney General (1950–63 as Solicitor General, Attorney General 1963–68).

• Option 3 John Austin is famous for the "Command Theory of Law" / analytical school of jurisprudence, not the Rule of Law.

• Option 4 Amartya Sen (AK Sen) is a Nobel laureate economist known for welfare economics and the capability approach.

NOTE

• The idea of "equality before law" in Article 14 is of British origin, while "equal protection of the laws" is borrowed from the American Constitution.

• Article 14 applies to all persons, not merely citizens.

question: In which state is Vijay Stambh situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Vijay Stambh" (Tower of Victory) stands inside the Chittorgarh Fort in Rajasthan. (विजय स्तंभ — चित्तौड़गढ़, राजस्थान)

• It was built by Maharana Kumbha (Rana Kumbha) between 1440 and 1448 CE to commemorate his victory over Mahmud Khilji of Malwa in 1440.

• The tower is about 37 metres (122 feet) high, has nine storeys, and is richly carved with Hindu deities — it is sometimes called an "encyclopaedia of Hindu iconography" in stone.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Close by stands the Kirti Stambh (Tower of Fame), a 12th-century Jain tower dedicated to Adinath, the first Jain Tirthankara.

• Chittorgarh Fort is one of the six "Hill Forts of Rajasthan" inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013 (the others: Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Amber, Jaisalmer and Gagron).

• Chittorgarh is associated with Rani Padmini, Meera Bai, Rana Kumbha and Rana Sanga.

NOTE

• Rana Kumbha also built Kumbhalgarh Fort, whose boundary wall (about 36 km) is often called the "Great Wall of India"; it is the birthplace of Maharana Pratap.

question: Which state passed a bill for the protection of advocates and became the first state to do so?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rajasthan became the first state in India to enact a law for the protection of advocates. The Rajasthan Advocates Protection Bill, 2023 was passed by the Rajasthan Assembly in March 2023. (अधिवक्ता संरक्षण विधेयक — राजस्थान)

• The law seeks to prevent acts of violence, assault, criminal force, intimidation and harassment against advocates while they discharge their professional duties, and provides for imprisonment and fine for offenders.

• The Bill was brought after lawyers across the state agitated following attacks on advocates.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The legal profession in India is regulated by the Advocates Act, 1961, under which the Bar Council of India (BCI) was set up.

• Rajasthan has also been in the news for other "firsts", such as the Right to Health Act, 2023, making it the first state to guarantee a legal right to health care.

NOTE

• Under the Seventh Schedule, "Administration of justice; constitution and organisation of all courts except the Supreme Court and High Courts" is in the Concurrent List (Entry 11A), which enables states to legislate on such matters.

question: Chaoite, Buckminsterfullerene and Graphene are related to which element?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carbon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chaoite, Buckminsterfullerene and Graphene are all allotropes of carbon. (कार्बन के अपररूप)

◦ Chaoite — a rare, hexagonal carbon mineral first reported from the Ries crater in Germany, believed to be formed by meteorite impact on graphite.

◦ Buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀) — a football-shaped molecule of 60 carbon atoms, discovered in 1985 by Kroto, Curl and Smalley (Nobel Prize in Chemistry, 1996), named after the architect Buckminster Fuller.

◦ Graphene — a single one-atom-thick layer of graphite; isolated in 2004 by Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov (Nobel Prize in Physics, 2010). It is the strongest known material and an excellent conductor.

• Allotropy is the existence of an element in two or more different physical forms in the same physical state.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other allotropes of carbon: diamond (hardest natural substance, sp³ hybridised, three-dimensional network), graphite (soft, good conductor, sp² hybridised layers, used as a lubricant and in pencils), carbon nanotubes, lonsdaleite, amorphous carbon (charcoal, coke, lamp black).

• Carbon: symbol C, atomic number 6, Group 14 of the periodic table; it is called the "king of the elements" because it forms the largest number of compounds (catenation).

NOTE

• Allotropes of other elements: oxygen (O₂ and ozone O₃), phosphorus (white, red, black), sulphur (rhombic, monoclinic, plastic), tin (grey and white).

question: Who is credited with the establishment of Servants of India Society?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Servants of India Society" was founded in 1905 at Pune by Gopal Krishna Gokhale. (भारत सेवक समाज — गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले, 1905)

• Its aim was to train national missionaries for the service of India and to promote, by constitutional means, the true interests of the Indian people — education, sanitation, famine relief and the uplift of tribals and depressed classes.

• Its journal was "Hitavada". After Gokhale’s death in 1915, Srinivasa Sastri led the Society.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (1866–1915) was a moderate leader of the Indian National Congress, its President at the Banaras session (1905), and the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi.

• Option 1 Lala Lajpat Rai founded the Servants of the People Society (Lok Sevak Mandal) in 1921 at Lahore — a common point of confusion in exams.

• Option 3 M. G. Ranade founded the Prarthana Samaj (1867) and the Indian National Social Conference (1887).

• Option 4 C. R. Das (Deshbandhu) co-founded the Swaraj Party (1923) with Motilal Nehru.

NOTE

• Gokhale was called "the Diamond of India" by Mahatma Gandhi; Gandhi wrote of him as his political mentor in his autobiography.

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak, the extremist leader, was Gokhale’s contemporary and rival within the Congress.

question: The value of all final goods and services produced within the country during one year is known as __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is gross domestic product.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gross Domestic Product (GDP)" is the market value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country during a given period (usually one year). (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद)

• The key word is "within the country" — GDP is measured on a territorial basis, irrespective of who owns the factors of production.

• Formula (expenditure method): GDP = C + I + G + (X – M), where C = private consumption, I = investment, G = government expenditure, X = exports and M = imports.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA) — it is measured on a national basis (income earned by a country’s residents wherever they are).

• NNP = GNP – Depreciation; NDP = GDP – Depreciation. "Net" always means after deducting depreciation (consumption of fixed capital).

• National Income = NNP at factor cost. Per capita income = National income ÷ Population.

NOTE

• In India, national income estimates are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

• The first attempt to estimate India’s national income was by Dadabhai Naoroji in "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" (1901); the first scientific estimate was by Prof. V. K. R. V. Rao (1931–32); after Independence, the National Income Committee (1949) was chaired by P. C. Mahalanobis.

question: Who was the first speaker of the Lok Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is GV Mavalankar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar (G. V. Mavalankar) was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha, holding office from 15 May 1952 to 27 February 1956. (लोक सभा के प्रथम अध्यक्ष)

• He is popularly called "Dadasaheb". Before becoming Speaker of the Lok Sabha, he was President of the Central Legislative Assembly and then Speaker of the Provisional Parliament (1950–52).

• He is regarded as the "Father of the Lok Sabha", a title given to him by Jawaharlal Nehru.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar was the second Speaker of the Lok Sabha (1956–62) and the first Deputy Speaker.

• Option 1 Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was Speaker (1967–69, 1977) and later became the 6th President of India; he is the only Speaker to become President.

• Option 4 Meira Kumar was the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha (2009–14).

NOTE

• The Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members (Article 93). While the office of Speaker is vacant, the duties are performed by the Deputy Speaker.

• The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by an effective majority after 14 days’ notice.

• The Speaker has a casting vote in case of a tie, decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill (Article 110), and presides over joint sittings of Parliament (Article 108).

question: ‘The Story of My Experiments with Truth’ is an autobiography of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Story of My Experiments with Truth" is the autobiography of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi (Mahatma Gandhi). (सत्य के साथ मेरे प्रयोग — महात्मा गांधी की आत्मकथा)

• It was originally written in Gujarati and published in weekly instalments in the journal "Navjivan" between 1925 and 1929. It was translated into English by Mahadev Desai.

• The book covers Gandhi’s life from his birth in 1869 up to about 1921, describing his experiments with truth (satya), non-violence (ahimsa), brahmacharya, diet and Satyagraha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other works by Gandhi: "Hind Swaraj" (1909), "My Experiments with Truth", "Satyagraha in South Africa", "Key to Health", "Unto This Last: A Paraphrase (Sarvodaya)".

• Gandhi edited the journals Young India, Navjivan, Harijan and (in South Africa) Indian Opinion.

• Option 1 Dr Rajendra Prasad’s autobiography is "Atmakatha"; he was India’s first President.

• Option 4 Jawaharlal Nehru wrote "An Autobiography (Toward Freedom)", "The Discovery of India" and "Glimpses of World History".

NOTE

• Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 at Porbandar, Gujarat; his birthday is observed as Gandhi Jayanti and as the International Day of Non-Violence (declared by the UN in 2007).

• He was given the title "Mahatma" by Rabindranath Tagore, and Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose called him the "Father of the Nation".

question: Who was the music director of the famous film ‘Sholay’ released in 1975?
solution_text:
The correct answer is RD Burman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rahul Dev Burman (R. D. Burman), affectionately called "Pancham da", composed the music for the blockbuster film "Sholay" (1975). (शोले — संगीतकार आर. डी. बर्मन)

• Famous songs from Sholay include "Yeh Dosti Hum Nahin Todenge", "Mehbooba Mehbooba" (sung by R. D. Burman himself) and "Holi Ke Din", with lyrics by Anand Bakshi.

• "Sholay" was directed by Ramesh Sippy, written by Salim–Javed, and starred Dharmendra, Amitabh Bachchan, Hema Malini, Sanjeev Kumar and Amjad Khan (as Gabbar Singh).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• R. D. Burman was the son of the legendary composer Sachin Dev Burman (S. D. Burman). He won the Filmfare Award for Best Music Director for "Sanam Teri Kasam", "Masoom" and "1942: A Love Story".

• Option 1 Madan Mohan was renowned for ghazals in films such as "Anpadh", "Woh Kaun Thi" and "Heer Raanjha".

• Option 2 Jatin–Lalit composed for "Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge", "Kuch Kuch Hota Hai" and "Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar" in the 1990s.

• Option 3 Nadeem–Shravan became famous with "Aashiqui" (1990) and "Raja Hindustani".

NOTE

• "Sholay" is often described as one of the greatest Indian films ever made; it ran for five years continuously at the Minerva theatre, Mumbai, and was among the earliest Indian films with stereophonic sound and 70 mm presentation.

question: The technique of classical dancing was codified by ______________ in about the 5th century B.C.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharata.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The technique and grammar of Indian classical dance and drama were codified by the sage Bharata (Bharata Muni) in his treatise "Natya Shastra". (नाट्य शास्त्र — भरत मुनि)

• The Natya Shastra is the oldest surviving text on dramaturgy, dance, music and aesthetics in India; it is often dated between the 5th century BCE and the 2nd century CE.

• It elaborates the theory of "Rasa" (aesthetic flavour) and "Bhava" (emotion), the nine rasas (Navarasa), hand gestures (hastas/mudras), body movements (angikabhinaya), and the four kinds of abhinaya — Angika, Vachika, Aharya and Sattvika.

• Because it combines the elements of the four Vedas, it is sometimes called the "Fifth Veda (Panchama Veda)".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Sudraka was the author of the Sanskrit play "Mrichchhakatika (The Little Clay Cart)".

• Option 3 Chanakya (Kautilya/Vishnugupta) wrote the "Arthashastra", a treatise on statecraft and economics.

• Option 4 Kalhana wrote "Rajatarangini", a chronicle of the kings of Kashmir (12th century).

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

• Nandikeshvara’s "Abhinaya Darpana" is another important text on dance gestures.

question: Who among the following is the author of the novel ‘Animal Farm’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is George Orwell.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Animal Farm" (1945) is a political allegorical novella written by George Orwell — the pen name of Eric Arthur Blair. (एनिमल फार्म — जॉर्ज ऑरवेल)

• The story of farm animals who overthrow their human owner is a satire on the Russian Revolution of 1917 and the rise of Stalinism. Its most quoted line is: "All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others."

• Orwell was born in Motihari, Bihar (India) in 1903 and served in the Indian Imperial Police in Burma.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Orwell’s other famous work is "Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984)", which gave the world the terms Big Brother, Thought Police, doublethink and Newspeak. He also wrote "Burmese Days", "Homage to Catalonia" and "The Road to Wigan Pier".

• Option 1 Thomas Hardy wrote "Tess of the d’Urbervilles", "Far from the Madding Crowd" and "The Mayor of Casterbridge".

• Option 3 Roald Dahl wrote children’s classics such as "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory", "Matilda" and "The BFG".

• Option 4 Charles Dickens wrote "Oliver Twist", "A Tale of Two Cities", "David Copperfield" and "Great Expectations".

NOTE

• The adjective "Orwellian" describes a totalitarian society marked by surveillance, propaganda and the denial of truth.

question: Who among the following is credited with starting a Fusion Dance form called ‘Hi-Dance’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uday Shankar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Uday Shankar (1900–1977) is credited with creating a fusion (or "Hi-Dance") style that blended Indian classical and folk dance with European theatrical and ballet techniques. (उदय शंकर — फ्यूजन नृत्य के प्रवर्तक)

• He is regarded as the father of modern dance in India. He founded the Uday Shankar India Culture Centre at Almora (1938) and produced the celebrated dance film "Kalpana" (1948).

• He performed with the Russian ballerina Anna Pavlova in Europe, creating pieces such as "Radha–Krishna".

• He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan (1971) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Uday Shankar was the elder brother of the sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar; his son Ananda Shankar was a noted fusion musician and his daughter-in-law Mamata Shankar and wife Amala Shankar were dancers.

• Option 1 Shashadhar Acharya is a well-known exponent of Chhau (Seraikella style) dance.

• Option 3 Kartik Ram was a famous Raigarh gharana Kathak dancer of Chhattisgarh.

• Option 4 Mani Damodara (Mani Madhava Chakyar’s tradition/Kathakali circles) is associated with Kerala’s classical performing arts.

NOTE

• The Uday Shankar Nritya Utsav is held annually in Kolkata in his memory.

• Other pioneers of modern Indian dance: Rukmini Devi Arundale (revived Bharatanatyam, founded Kalakshetra) and Rabindranath Tagore (Rabindra Nritya Natya).

question: According to the Census of India 2011, which of the following states has the lowest population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, Sikkim is the least populated state of India, with a population of about 6.11 lakh (610,577). (सिक्किम — सबसे कम जनसंख्या वाला राज्य)

• Ascending order of population among the smallest states (2011): Sikkim (6.11 lakh) < Mizoram (10.97 lakh) < Arunachal Pradesh (13.84 lakh) < Goa (14.59 lakh) < Nagaland (19.79 lakh) < Manipur (28.56 lakh).

• Among Union Territories, Lakshadweep had the lowest population (about 64,473).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Uttar Pradesh was the most populous state (about 19.98 crore), followed by Maharashtra, Bihar, West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh.

• Sikkim is also the second smallest state by area (7,096 sq km) after Goa (3,702 sq km).

• Census 2011 figures: total population 121.09 crore; density 382 persons per sq km; sex ratio 943; literacy 74.04%; decadal growth 17.7%.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th Census since 1872 and the 7th after Independence.

• Highest density: Bihar (1,106); lowest density: Arunachal Pradesh (17). Highest literacy: Kerala (93.91%); lowest: Bihar (61.80%).

question: The Lambadi dance is a folk dance form of the ____________ tribe and originated in Andhra Pradesh.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Banjara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lambadi" is a colourful folk dance of the Banjara (Lambadi/Lambani) tribe, originating in Andhra Pradesh and also performed in Telangana, Karnataka and Rajasthan. (लंबाडी नृत्य — बंजारा जनजाति)

• It is performed mainly by women to celebrate a good harvest or a successful sowing season, and is marked by elaborate costumes with mirror work, ivory bangles, heavy silver jewellery and embroidered skirts.

• The Banjaras are traditionally a nomadic community believed to have migrated from Rajasthan/Marwar, historically engaged in the transport of goods (salt and grain) by bullock caravans.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Sugali is one of the local names by which the same community is known in parts of Andhra Pradesh, but the dance is universally identified with the Banjara tribe.

• Options 3 Nakkala and 4 Dabba Yerukula are other Scheduled Tribes of Andhra Pradesh, not associated with Lambadi.

NOTE

• Other folk dances of Andhra Pradesh: Kuchipudi (classical), Veeranatyam, Butta Bommalu, Dhimsa, Tappeta Gullu, Burrakatha, Kolattam.

• Folk dances to remember for SSC: Bihu (Assam), Garba/Dandiya (Gujarat), Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Ghoomar/Kalbelia (Rajasthan), Lavani (Maharashtra), Chhau (Jharkhand–Odisha–West Bengal), Bamboo dance/Cheraw (Mizoram), Rouf (Jammu & Kashmir).

question: In which of the following years was the Child Marriage Restraint Act passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1929.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Child Marriage Restraint Act" was passed in 1929 and came into force on 1 April 1930. It is popularly known as the "Sarda Act" after its sponsor Rai Sahib Harbilas Sarda, a member of the Central Legislative Assembly from Ajmer. (शारदा अधिनियम, 1929)

• It fixed the minimum age of marriage at 14 years for girls and 18 years for boys. In 1978 the ages were raised to 18 for girls and 21 for boys.

• The Act was passed during the viceroyalty of Lord Irwin.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 1856 — the Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act, passed largely because of the efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, during the time of Lord Canning.

• Option 3 1878 — the Vernacular Press Act (Lord Lytton), which restricted Indian-language newspapers, and the Arms Act.

• The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 has replaced the 1929 Act and makes child marriage voidable and punishable.

NOTE

• Other social reform legislation of the colonial era:

◦ 1829 — Abolition of Sati (Lord William Bentinck, with Raja Ram Mohan Roy).

◦ 1843 — Abolition of slavery (Lord Ellenborough).

◦ 1856 — Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act.

◦ 1891 — Age of Consent Act (raised the age of consent for girls to 12).

question: What is the main reason behind the substantial rainfall during summer on the western coasts of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Western Ghats.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The heavy rainfall on India’s western coast during the summer monsoon is caused mainly by the Western Ghats, which lie perpendicular (at right angles) to the moisture-laden south-west monsoon winds coming from the Arabian Sea. (पश्चिमी घाट — वृष्टि छाया व orographic वर्षा)

• The mountains force the moist air to rise, cool and condense, producing very heavy orographic (relief) rainfall on the windward (western) slopes — over 250–400 cm in places such as Mahabaleshwar and Agumbe.

• The leeward (eastern) side — the Deccan Plateau — lies in the rain shadow and gets far less rain (e.g. Pune, Sholapur, Bijapur).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The south-west monsoon enters India in two branches — the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch — and normally reaches Kerala around 1 June.

• The Eastern Ghats are parallel to the Bay of Bengal branch of the monsoon and are also discontinuous and lower, so they cause little orographic rainfall; the Coromandel coast gets most of its rain from the retreating (north-east) monsoon in October–December.

NOTE

• Highest peaks: Anamudi (2,695 m) in the Western Ghats (highest peak of peninsular India) and Arma Konda/Jindhagada in the Eastern Ghats.

• The Western Ghats (Sahyadri) are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the world’s eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity.

question: The second edition of Khelo India Youth Games, 2019 was organised in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pune.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The second edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) 2019 was held at Pune, Maharashtra, in January 2019. (खेलो इंडिया यूथ गेम्स 2019 — पुणे)

• Maharashtra topped the medal tally at these Games. The mascot was "Jaadu".

• The first edition (2018), then called the Khelo India School Games, was held in New Delhi, where Haryana finished first.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Editions of the Khelo India Youth Games:

◦ 2018 — New Delhi (Haryana champion)

◦ 2019 — Pune, Maharashtra (Maharashtra champion)

◦ 2020 — Guwahati, Assam (Maharashtra champion)

◦ 2021/22 — Panchkula, Haryana (Haryana champion)

◦ 2022/23 — Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal and other cities) (Maharashtra champion)

◦ 2023/24 — Tamil Nadu (Chennai and others) (Maharashtra champion)

• The Khelo India Programme was launched in 2018 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to revive sports culture at the grassroots level.

NOTE

• Related events under the scheme: Khelo India University Games, Khelo India Winter Games (held in Ladakh and Jammu & Kashmir) and Khelo India Para Games.

question: ACF conferred Grandmaster ________ with Player of the Year award, who is only the sixth Indian to break the 2700 Elo-rating mark and the youngest Grandmaster from the country to be rated above 2700.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D Gukesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dommaraju Gukesh (D Gukesh) of Chennai, Tamil Nadu, was named Player of the Year by the Asian Chess Federation (ACF). (डी. गुकेश — शतरंज ग्रैंडमास्टर)

• He became only the sixth Indian to cross the 2700 Elo-rating mark and the youngest Indian Grandmaster to be rated above 2700.

• Gukesh became a Grandmaster in 2019 at the age of 12 years, 7 months and 17 days, then the second youngest GM in history.

• The other Indians who had crossed 2700 before him: Viswanathan Anand, P. Harikrishna, Vidit Gujrathi, B. Adhiban and Krishnan Sasikiran.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In 2023 Gukesh overtook Viswanathan Anand to become India’s top-rated player, ending Anand’s 36-year reign.

• He was a member of the Indian team that won bronze at the 44th Chess Olympiad (Chennai, 2022), where he won an individual gold on board one.

• The Elo rating system was devised by the Hungarian-American physicist Arpad Elo.

NOTE

• Viswanathan Anand was India’s first Grandmaster (1988) and a five-time World Chess Champion; he was the first recipient of the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (1991–92).

• World chess is governed by FIDE (Fédération Internationale des Échecs), founded in 1924 at Paris. International Chess Day is observed on 20 July.

question: Which condition causes bone pain, poor growth, and soft, weak bones that can lead to bone deformities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rickets.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rickets" is a disease of children caused by a deficiency of Vitamin D (calciferol), calcium or phosphorus. It leads to soft, weak bones, bone pain, poor growth and skeletal deformities such as bow legs, knock knees and a deformed rib cage (rickety rosary). (रिकेट्स — विटामिन D की कमी)

• The corresponding disease in adults is "osteomalacia", in which the bones become soft and painful.

• Vitamin D is synthesised in the skin on exposure to sunlight (UV-B rays); hence it is called the "sunshine vitamin".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 Cerebral palsy is a group of disorders affecting movement, muscle tone and posture, caused by damage to the developing brain.

• Option 3 Pertussis is "whooping cough", a bacterial respiratory infection caused by Bordetella pertussis; it is covered by the DPT vaccine.

• Option 4 Asplenia means the absence of normal spleen function, which increases the risk of serious infection.

NOTE

• Vitamin deficiency diseases frequently asked in SSC exams:

◦ Vitamin A (Retinol) — night blindness, xerophthalmia.

◦ Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) — beri-beri; B2 (Riboflavin) — cheilosis; B3 (Niacin) — pellagra; B12 (Cobalamin) — pernicious anaemia.

◦ Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) — scurvy.

◦ Vitamin D (Calciferol) — rickets/osteomalacia.

◦ Vitamin E (Tocopherol) — sterility; Vitamin K (Phylloquinone) — delayed blood clotting.

• Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K; the rest (B-complex and C) are water-soluble.

question: In which Indian musician’s name did the state of Massachusetts in the USA declare April 20th in 1984 as a day in his name?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amjad Ali Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The state of Massachusetts (USA) declared 20 April 1984 as "Amjad Ali Khan Day" in honour of the celebrated Indian sarod maestro Ustad Amjad Ali Khan. (उस्ताद अमजद अली खान — सरोद वादक)

• He belongs to the Senia Bangash gharana and is a sixth-generation musician; his ancestor Ghulam Bandegi Khan Bangash is credited with developing the sarod from the Afghan rabab.

• He was also given the honorary citizenship of Houston, Texas (1997) and Massachusetts’ recognition made him one of the first Indian musicians so honoured in the USA.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Amjad Ali Khan has received the Padma Shri (1975), Padma Bhushan (1991), Padma Vibhushan (2001), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and the UNESCO Music Prize (1970) as well as the UNICEF National Ambassadorship.

• His sons Amaan Ali Bangash and Ayaan Ali Bangash are also sarod players.

• Option 2 Ali Akbar Khan was another legendary sarod player, son of Allauddin Khan of the Maihar gharana.

• Option 1 Brij Narayan is a sarod player, son of Pandit Ram Narayan (sarangi); Option 3 Rajeev Taranath was a distinguished sarod exponent and disciple of Ali Akbar Khan.

NOTE

• Instrument–artist pairs for SSC: Sitar — Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan; Sarod — Amjad Ali Khan, Ali Akbar Khan; Shehnai — Bismillah Khan; Santoor — Shivkumar Sharma; Flute — Hariprasad Chaurasia; Tabla — Zakir Hussain, Alla Rakha; Sarangi — Ram Narayan; Violin — L. Subramaniam; Mandolin — U. Srinivas; Veena — S. Balachander.

question: Which of the following is an advantage of microfinance institutions in India?
option_2: Increased reliance on informal lending sources
solution_text:
The correct answer is Enhanced financial inclusion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Microfinance Institutions (MFIs)" provide small loans, savings, insurance and other financial services to low-income households and micro-entrepreneurs who have no access to formal banking. (सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थान — वित्तीय समावेशन)

• Their biggest advantage is therefore "enhanced financial inclusion" — bringing the unbanked poor, especially rural households and women, into the formal financial system.

• Other advantages: they reduce dependence on moneylenders, promote self-employment and women’s empowerment, and help in poverty alleviation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 all state negatives, which are the opposite of the benefits of microfinance:

◦ MFIs are intended to increase the impact on poverty reduction, reduce reliance on informal moneylenders and maximise support for women entrepreneurs.

• In India, MFIs are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI); many operate as NBFC-MFIs. The SHG–Bank Linkage Programme was launched by NABARD in 1992.

• Bandhan Bank began as a microfinance institution before becoming a universal bank.

NOTE

• The Grameen Bank of Bangladesh, founded by Prof. Muhammad Yunus, pioneered modern microfinance; Yunus and the bank shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.

• Related financial-inclusion schemes: PMJDY (2014), PM MUDRA Yojana (2015), Stand-Up India (2016), PM SVANidhi (2020).

question: Which of the following statements about Mahatma Gandhi is INCORRECT?
option_1: Mahatma Gandhi was born in 1869 in Porbandar.
option_2: In 1942, he launched the Quit India Movement.
option_3: He led the Champaran Satyagraha in 1910.
option_4: He led the Dandi Salt March in 1930.
solution_text:
The correct answer is He led the Champaran Satyagraha in 1910.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The statement in Option 3 is INCORRECT. The Champaran Satyagraha took place in 1917, not 1910. (चंपारण सत्याग्रह — 1917)

• It was Gandhi’s first Satyagraha in India, launched in Champaran district of Bihar at the request of the indigo cultivator Raj Kumar Shukla, against the oppressive "tinkathia system" under which peasants were forced to grow indigo on 3/20 of their land.

• Gandhi had returned to India from South Africa in January 1915, so he could not have led any movement in India in 1910.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is correct — Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 at Porbandar, Gujarat.

• Option 2 is correct — the Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 from the Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, with the slogan "Do or Die".

• Option 4 is correct — the Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) began on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram and ended at Dandi on 6 April 1930, covering about 385 km with 78 followers.

NOTE

• Gandhi’s major movements: Champaran (1917), Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918), Kheda Satyagraha (1918), Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919), Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22), Civil Disobedience Movement (1930–34), Quit India Movement (1942).

• Gandhi presided over only one Congress session — Belgaum, 1924.

question: Which university won the first place in the 3rd Khelo India University Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Panjab University.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Panjab University, Chandigarh finished first in the 3rd Khelo India University Games (KIUG), held in Uttar Pradesh in May–June 2023. (खेलो इंडिया यूनिवर्सिटी गेम्स — पंजाब यूनिवर्सिटी)

• Panjab University topped the medal tally with 26 gold medals among a total of about 69 medals, ahead of Guru Nanak Dev University, Amritsar and Jain University, Bengaluru.

• The Games were hosted across Varanasi, Lucknow, Gorakhpur, Noida and Delhi, with the mascot "Jeetu".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Winners of the Khelo India University Games:

◦ 1st edition (2020, Bhubaneswar, Odisha) — Panjab University.

◦ 2nd edition (2021/22, Bengaluru, Karnataka) — Jain University, Bengaluru.

◦ 3rd edition (2023, Uttar Pradesh) — Panjab University.

◦ 4th edition (2024, Guwahati, Assam) — Chandigarh University.

• The Khelo India University Games are conducted by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports along with the Association of Indian Universities (AIU).

NOTE

• Panjab University was established in 1882 at Lahore and, after Partition, was re-established in India; it is now located at Chandigarh.

question: In which of the following states of India is the maximum extent of alluvial soil found?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alluvial soil covers the largest area in Uttar Pradesh, because almost the whole state lies in the vast Indo-Gangetic plain built by the deposits of the Ganga, Yamuna, Ghaghara, Gomti and Ramganga. (जलोढ़ मिट्टी — उत्तर प्रदेश)

• Alluvial soil is the most widespread soil of India, covering about 40 per cent of the total land area, and is the most fertile, being rich in potash, phosphoric acid and lime but deficient in nitrogen and humus.

• Two types:

◦ "Khadar" — new alluvium, found near river banks, renewed every year by floods, more fertile.

◦ "Bhangar" — old alluvium, on higher ground, often containing lime nodules called "kankar".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Crops grown on alluvial soil: wheat, rice, sugarcane, pulses, oilseeds and jute.

• Black soil (regur) is dominant in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Telangana and Karnataka — it is formed from lava and is ideal for cotton.

• Red soil is found in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh and Odisha; laterite soil in the Western Ghats, Kerala and Meghalaya (good for tea, coffee, cashew).

NOTE

• Soil classification in India is done by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), which recognises eight major soil types: alluvial, black, red, laterite, arid/desert, saline/alkaline, peaty/marshy and forest soils.

question: The ________ port was developed after Independence to ease the volume of trade on the Mumbai port.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kandla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kandla Port, situated on the Gulf of Kachchh in Gujarat, was developed soon after Independence to relieve the pressure of traffic on Mumbai (Bombay) port and to serve as the chief port for western and north-western India after Karachi went to Pakistan in 1947. (कांडला बंदरगाह — गुजरात)

• It is a tidal port and India’s first Special Economic Zone (Kandla SEZ, 1965) was set up here. It handles large quantities of petroleum, chemicals, fertilisers, salt and textiles.

• It was renamed the "Deendayal Port" in 2017.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva), opened in 1989 near Mumbai, was also built to decongest Mumbai port and is India’s largest container-handling port.

• Option 2 Kolkata is India’s only major riverine port, on the Hooghly; Option 3 Chennai is one of the oldest artificial ports on the east coast; Option 4 Visakhapatnam is India’s deepest port, in Andhra Pradesh.

NOTE

• India has about 12–13 major ports. On the west coast: Kandla (Deendayal), Mumbai, JNPT, Mormugao, New Mangalore, Cochin. On the east coast: Kolkata–Haldia, Paradip, Visakhapatnam, Kamarajar (Ennore), Chennai, V. O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin), and Port Blair in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

• Major ports are administered by the Centre under the Major Port Authorities Act, 2021.
